Trade
trād
n. and v. (one's occupation; commerce; to traffic; rendering Hebrew sachar and the phrase men of cattle, Greek ergazomai and diapragmateuomai)
Middle Low German trade, a track, course; a trade is the path a man goes up and down. The Hebrew of Genesis 34 is to go about as a merchant.

Biblical Definition

Hamor to Jacob's sons: “dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions” (Gen 34:10; Gen 34:21). Joseph of his brothers: “their trade hath been to feed cattle” (Gen 46:32), and their answer to Pharaoh, “Thy servants' trade hath been about cattle from our youth even until now” (Gen 46:34). The servant with five talents “went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents” (Mat 25:16); the nobleman returned to know “how much every man had gained by trading” (Luk 19:15). At Babylon's fall, “every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off” (Rev 18:17).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines trade as the act or business of exchanging commodities; the business which a person has learned and which he carries on for procuring subsistence or for profit; occupation.

expand to see more

TRADE, n. The act or business of exchanging commodities by barter, or by buying and selling for money; commerce; traffick.

2. The business which a person has learned, and which he carries on for procuring subsistence or for profit; occupation; particularly, mechanical employment.

TRADE, v.i. To barter, or to buy and sell; to traffick; to carry on commerce.

Key Scripture

Mat 25:16 — "Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents."

Luk 19:15 — "And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading."

Gen 46:34 — "That ye shall say, Thy servants' trade hath been about cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and also our fathers: that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians."

Gen 34:10 — "And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you; dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein."

Rev 18:17 — "For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off,"

Modern Corruption

The buried talent is defended as prudence, and the Lord called the servant who would not trade wicked and slothful.

expand to see more

The parable of the talents turns on a verb. The first servant went and traded, and the second, and they were welcomed with the same words; the third buried his lord's money in the earth, and his defence was caution — I was afraid — and the sentence was the outer darkness. What is entrusted to a servant of Christ is not given to be kept safe but to be put to work, at risk, in the market, and the man who has preserved his gift unspent has not been faithful but afraid, and the Lord calls that wicked. Genesis 47 is trade at the other end: Jacob's sons told Pharaoh their trade was cattle, an abomination to Egypt, and the honest answer got them a land of their own. Revelation 18:17 is trade's last scene, the shipmasters standing afar off as Babylon burns, weeping for the market that was.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sachar (H5503), to go about, trade; anshei miqneh (H582, H4735), men of cattle; Greek ergazomai (G2038), to work, trade; diapragmateuomai (G1281), to gain by trading.

expand to see more

Hebrew sachar (H5503) — to trade, traffic; Genesis 34:10, 34:21, 42:34; anshei miqneh (H582, H4735), men of cattle, whose trade is cattle; Genesis 46:32, 46:34.

Greek ergazomai (G2038) — to work, trade; Matthew 25:16, Revelation 18:17; diapragmateuomai (G1281), Luke 19:15.

Usage

"“Went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents” — the gift put to work at risk."

"“Thy servants' trade hath been about cattle” — the honest answer that got them Goshen."

"“As many as trade by sea, stood afar off” — the market's grief at Babylon."
